steps: Check location & permits
Freestanding room heater for an insulated, habitable room — never a sleeping room. Ask local building or fire officials about permits and inspection first.

Listed as a freestanding solid-fuel room heater, certified for the USA and Canada and approved for mobile homes (USA) and transportable buildings (CAN). Ask local building or fire officials about restrictions, permits and inspection before you start.

It is designed for insulated, habitable rooms — not a concrete, uninsulated basement or a shop/garage, where constant over-firing voids the warranty (p. 16). Never install it in a bedroom or any area used for sleeping.

Note: the certification label says the stove is not to be installed in any fireplace (p. 4); p. 13 says not to install it in an alcove or fireplace in Canada and, in the USA, to adhere to minimum safe clearance dimensions. p. 14 lists the rear shield kit and fan kit as required for alcove installations.
Clearances & floor protection
Hold the lettered minimums from the clearance drawing. On a combustible floor, use a non-combustible floor shield — in the USA, 16" in front and 8" either side of the loading door.
Plan combustion air
In an airtight home, balance intake air for every exhausting appliance; a fresh air intake into the room is recommended. Don't tie into air distribution ductwork unless approved.
Connector & prefab chimney
6" 24 MSG steel connector to a 6" listed UL-103HT / CAN/ULC-S629 chimney. Screw every joint, use a support package or listed wall thimble, and never share a flue.

Use a 6" 24 MSG steel connector (no aluminum or galvanized) to a 6" listed factory-built chimney, UL-103HT (USA) or CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN). Fasten every joint with sheet metal screws; use a chimney support package through a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall. Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance.

Buy every prefab component (ceiling support or wall pass-through and "T", fire stops, insulation shield, flashing, cap) from the same chimney maker and follow its clearances. Running the chimney inside, up through the ceilings and roof, is recommended; if it has to run outside, build a chase around it.

Above the roof penetrationat least 3 ft
Above roof or obstruction within 10 ft (horizontal)at least 2 ft

Keep an effective vapor barrier where the chimney penetrates the exterior structure. In a creosote fire, chimney temperatures may exceed 2000F.
Masonry chimney (if used)
Have it inspected by a certified professional and cleaned first — no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage. A stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended.

Have the masonry chimney inspected by a certified professional to NFPA minimum standards: no cracks, no loose mortar, no signs of deterioration or blockage. Clean it before installing the stove. Blaze King recommends a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, to help maintain draft.

Passing the connector through a combustible wall needs special methods approved by your jurisdiction — NFPA minimum standards in the USA, CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada.
Set the chimney height
At least 15 ft from stove top to termination at 0–1000 ft elevation, more for altitude, elbows, a "T" or horizontal runs. No more than one offset (two elbows).
Mobile home extras
Roof exit only, with an outside air kit plus a fan kit or rear shield kit, double wall close-clearance pipe and a listed chimney. Fasten it to the floor with the kit's tie-downs.

• Install the kits before the stove: outside air kit (S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B) and either a fan kit (S.Z2514) or a rear shield kit (S.Z4015).
  • Flue pipe must be double wall, close clearance type with CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610 designation — no single wall pipe. Chimney: listed factory built, CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN) or UL-103HT (USA). Follow the chimney maker's instructions exactly and buy the ceiling support package from the same maker.
  • The fresh air hose must feed up into the intake channel on the rear of the stove — never through a wall above the bottom of that channel.
  • Fasten the stove to the floor with the tie-downs supplied in the outside air kit; remove both side shields to reach the holes.
  • Keep the floor, wall and ceiling/roof structurally sound, and never install in an area used for sleeping. The chimney must be removed to transport the building.
Note: for a mobile home install, pp. 4, 8 and 13 call for an outside air kit plus a fan kit or a rear shield kit; p. 14 describes the rear shield kit and the fan kit each as "required for mobile home or alcove installations."
Accessories, side shields & door
Fan kit: grounded three-prong plug into a grounded receptacle, cord never in front of or under the stove. Take the bypass handle off before the right side shield.

Fan kit power: plug straight into a properly grounded three-hole receptacle. Don't cut or remove the grounding prong, and don't route the cord in front of or under the stove.

Side shield removal

  1. Remove the two top screws and lift off the side shield cover plate.
  2. Remove the remaining 4 screws.
  3. Grasp the shield at the upper and lower cut-outs and lift it off (remove the bypass handle first for the right shield).
  4. Reverse to reinstall.

Loading door removal (p. 15)

Hold the shoulder bolt on top of the upper hinge with a 1/4" allen key and the nut below with a 9/16" wrench; turn the bolt counter-clockwise to remove the nut. Repeat on the lower hinge, then hold the door and pull the bolts. Reverse to install. Never operate the stove with the loading door off or open.
Hand over
Complete the installer notes on the last page, leave the manual with the homeowner, and remind them to mail the warranty registration card.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build the fire right on the bottom firebrick — never use a grate. Stay with the stove while the fire gets going.

  1. Check that all the bricks are in place inside the firebox.
  2. Turn the thermostat to High and the fan (if you have one) off.
  3. Open the bypass, then the loading door.
  4. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front and criss-cross 20 pieces of kindling on top, leaving air gaps.
  5. Light it and let it get a good start with the door cracked open.
  6. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  7. Latch the door. Once the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass.
  8. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads Active, open the bypass and door and fill the stove, wood as far back as possible. Latch the door and close the bypass.
  9. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down gradually.
Turned it down too far, too fast? If the fire dies down or the needle drops to Inactive, turn the thermostat back up and let the fire re-establish.
Note: the lighting steps say both to turn the fan on to high when you close the bypass and to turn it on after the initial warm-up (p. 20); p. 16 says to keep the fan off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass and thermometer
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

It's at the upper right rear corner. At High the stove burns fastest and gives the most heat; turn it counter-clockwise for less. Make changes gradually — a sudden change can make the thermostat work poorly. The minimum low burn setting is set at the factory and must not be altered.

Bypass handle

It's on the right side. Pointing forward, the bypass is open and smoke goes around the catalytic combustor — you open it to light and to reload. To close it, turn the handle clockwise until it points to the rear, then push down until you hear a click.

Catalytic thermometer

It sits on top and shows whether the combustor is working. Keep the needle in the Active zone. Inactive means the combustor is below 500F and isn't burning clean.

Have the optional fan? About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match its speed to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

Note: p. 18 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before you read the thermometer; pp. 29 and 35 say 10 minutes.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Check the thermometer first. If the needle is still Active, follow these steps; if it has dropped to Inactive, use the lighting steps instead. Little wood left or a cooling room are signs it's time, too.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait a few minutes for the airflow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes — this helps keep smoke out of the room.
  3. Crack the loading door to let room air in; give it a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If smoke spills, close the door a little until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn it down.

Fill it as full as you need — the wood only burns at the rate the thermostat is set. Load only within the area the manual shows shaded in its diagram on p. 19; loading beyond it voids the warranty. On low you may see little flame; that's fine while the needle stays Active.

Creosote on the glass after long, very low burns? Run the stove on High for about 30 minutes to burn most of it off.

normal.title: That smell, smoke or sound is probably normal
normal.html:
Paint smell and smoke at first

The first time the stove heats up, the paint cures and gives off a strong odor with some smoke. Burn at a low setting for several hours and open a door or window until it clears. The paint may change color too; it evens out after a few more fires.

Creaks and ticks

Minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts, and the noise it makes, is normal.

Little flame on low

On lower settings you may see little flame. If the thermometer stays Active, the burn is carrying on.

The thermometer climbs after you turn it down

Turning the thermostat down, especially early in a burn, makes more smoke — fuel for the combustor — so its temperature can rise for up to several hours. That's normal.

Smoke at the door on mild days

In spring and fall, around 55F to 70F outside, the chimney draws less and some smoke may spill when you open the door. Run on High for 30 minutes after lighting or reloading, and build smaller, hotter fires rather than turning the thermostat down.

Vapor from the chimney

It's mostly water vapor. In extreme cold it can freeze in some outside chimneys, even blocking them and putting the fire out — burn on High for 5 to 10 minutes to melt any ice.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural cordwood only. Hardwood and softwood both burn well; denser hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

  • Use seasoned wood: split, stacked so air reaches it, and kept out of rain and snow for at least 24 months. Aim for 20% moisture or lower.
  • Never burn wet, green or unseasoned wood. It wastes heat and can cause excessive creosote buildup. If that ignites, it can cause a chimney fire that may become a house fire and cause serious bodily harm.
  • Don't use offcuts, pressed logs or lots of small, very dry pieces as your main fuel — too much of them can overheat and damage the firebox.
  • Never burn treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Never burn flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel.
  • Never burn salt-water driftwood. It's very corrosive and will deteriorate the structure of the stove, and burning it will void the warranty.
  • Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one down the middle.
  2. On the split face, take readings 2" from each end and in the middle, pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings — it's an approximate guide.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to burn on High for a while after each reload. Moisture driven out of fresh wood causes much of the creosote on the glass. Leaving the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it low for an overnight burn also helps.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool — never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth, and no abrasive cleaners.
  • After any cleaner, rinse the glass well with water. Leftover cleaner bakes on and can be very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket seal is broken. The warranty covers thermal breakage only — not glass that's been struck, hit by wood sticking out of the door, or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners.

Replacement glass must be 5 mm ceramic glass.

ash.title: Ashes and routine care
ash.html:
Wait until the fire is out and the stove is cool. Take ashes out whenever they come within one inch of the door opening, but leave a bed about 1/2" thick — wood burns best on it. The supplied fire poker has a hook for removing the ash plug.

  • Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, and nothing else in it.
  • Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  • Keep them in the closed container until every cinder is cold, even if you'll bury or spread them.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases, which can cause suffocation.

Through the season

  • Look over the combustor and clean it as needed.
  • Check the thermometer's calibration, the thermostat, the fan and all gaskets.
  • Inspect and clean the venting system.
  • After the last fire of the season, remove all ash from the firebox and ash drawer, and check inside for warped or damaged parts.

combustor.title: Caring for the catalytic combustor
combustor.html:
The combustor burns the smoke, so a healthy one means a cleaner, more efficient fire and less creosote. Never run the stove without it.

Keep an eye on it

  • Look it over at least three times a heating season. Don't take it out unless performance has dropped.
  • A healthy combustor holds the thermometer in the Active zone (over 500 F) and often goes past 1000 F.
  • Quick check: open the bypass, wait a few minutes and watch the chimney smoke, then close it. There should be clearly less smoke with the bypass closed.

If the needle won't reach Active

Burn a well-established fire for 1 hour, then set the thermostat to medium-low. After 5 minutes, check the needle. Repeat for at least 3 burn cycles. Still Inactive? Clean the combustor; if that doesn't help, it may need replacing — call your Blaze King dealer. The thermometer itself could also be off.

Cleaning

Only when the stove is cool. Lift off the flame shield and lightly brush the face with a soft paint brush, or pass a vacuum wand near it. Leave the combustor in place, never scrape it, and don't push anything into its cells. A hot fire is usually the best cleaner.

safety.title: Safety and chimney fires
safety.html:
• Keep at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows. If an alarm sounds, get everyone out.
  • The stove is hot while it's burning. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and anything else that can burn at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood within the safety clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the loading door closed; open it only to add wood.

If a chimney or run-away fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat fully counter-clockwise and make sure the loading door and bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire; use a fire extinguisher or garden hose if needed.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're sure the chimney isn't damaged.

Preventing one

Creosote forms when wood burns slowly, and wet wood makes it worse. Have the chimney and stove cleaned at least once a year, ideally by a professional sweep. Replace worn or hardened gaskets, and don't leave the door or bypass open too long. Chimney fire damage isn't covered by the warranty.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
For the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, on stoves bought from an authorized Blaze King dealer and installed in the USA or Canada.

Catalytic combustor6 years
Stove body and accessories (steel firebox parts)5 years
Fan assemblies, thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
All parts and materials, incl. paint finish1 year

Later years are shared. Combustor: no charge for the first 3 years, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% of the retail price in years 4, 5 and 6. Other parts covered past the first year: you pay 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4 and 80% in year 5.

Not covered

  • Gaskets and firebrick
  • Over-firing (warped plates, burnt-off paint)
  • Driftwood, salt-saturated or treated wood, or any fuel but cordwood
  • Chimney fire damage, and glass breakage that isn't thermal
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of noticing it, with proof of purchase. The warranty can't be transferred. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

Certified to the 2020 EPA particulate emission standards using crib wood (EPA test method 28R). Efficiency is determined by the B415.1-10 method and stated as HHV, but the manual prints no efficiency figure.

Maker's website: HHV Tested Efficiency 80.4%.

The minimum low burn rate is factory-set; altering it, or operating with the combustor deactivated or removed, is against federal regulations.

specFlue.title: Flue pipe and chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D.
Flue pipe6" diameter, 24 MSG steel
Not allowedaluminum or galvanized steel
Chimney6" listed factory built, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or code-compliant masonry with liner

A chimney connector is required; don't install the chimney directly at the outlet. Keep the flue pipe as direct as possible and inside the room — never through an attic or roof space, closet or other concealed space, floor or ceiling. Fasten every joint with sheet metal screws. Use a chimney support package through a ceiling to a listed prefab chimney, and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall. Double wall pipe from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box is recommended for freestanding installs.

Mobile home and residential close clearance installs need a 6" listed double wall, close clearance connector with a matching listed chimney. Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance (it also voids the warranty). In Canada, comply with CSA B365-M87.

specChimney.title: Minimum chimney height
specChimney.html:
Minimum recommended vertical height, stove top to termination, by elevation and elbows:

Elevation0 elbows · 2 x 15° · 2 x 30° · 2 x 45°
0 – 1000 ft15 · 16 · 18 · 19 ft
1000 – 2000 ft15.5 · 16.5 · 18.5 · 19.5 ft
2000 – 3000 ft16 · 17 · 19 · 20 ft
3000 – 4000 ft16.5 · 17.5 · 19.5 · 20.5 ft
4000 – 5000 ft17 · 18 · 20 · 21 ft
5000 – 6000 ft17.5 · 18.5 · 20.5 · 21.5 ft
6000 – 7000 ft18 · 19 · 21 · 22 ft
7000 – 8000 ft18.5 · 19.5 · 21.5 · 22.5 ft

No more than one offset (two elbows) is allowed; two 45° elbows equal one 90°. Add height for other parts: 90° elbow 2.0 ft; "T" section 3.0 ft; 1.0 ft of horizontal run = 2 ft of vertical rise. The manual's sea-level example: 15.0 ft + one 90° elbow 2.0 ft + 2.0' horizontal run 4.0 ft + one base "T" 3.0 ft = 24.0 ft. These are guidelines; draft also depends on local conditions. Above the roof: at least 3 ft higher than the highest point where it passes through the roof, and at least 2 ft higher than the highest part of the roof or any obstruction within 10 ft, measured horizontally (p. 10).

Note: p. 9 recommends a vertical rise of 3 ft from stove top to the first elbow for wall exits; the troubleshooting chart on p. 36 says to make certain a minimum vertical rise of 36" is observed prior to elbows.

specFloor.html:

On a combustible floornon-combustible floor shield

Canada (CSA B365): protect any combustible covering beneath the stove and at least 18" beyond any side with a door (across the full width of the stove plus the 8" on each side) and at least 8" beyond the other sides, with a continuous, durable, non-combustible pad that provides ember protection. Less than 8" from a wall, the pad need only reach the base of the wall. Don't put an ember pad on carpet unless it's structurally supported.

A non-combustible shield is also required under the chimney connector, extending at least 2" either side of it. p. 8 says that shield needs no insulation value but must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1), and gives the minimum sizes above in the same sentence; the label (p. 4) gives them as the minimum floor protection size. Blaze King doesn't recommend adhesive based vinyl flooring in front of the stove.

specAir.title: Combustion and outside air
specAir.html:
3" outside air kitS.Z1726B
4" outside air kitS.Z1726
Mobile homeoutside air kit required

In airtight homes, make sure there is enough intake air for every exhausting appliance — HRVs, constantly running air-handler fans, fireplaces, range hoods, dryers. A fresh air intake into the stove's room is recommended; without one you risk air starvation, smoke spillage and carbon monoxide (p. 9). Consult an HVAC specialist. Don't connect the stove to any air distribution ductwork unless specifically approved.

The kit's fresh air hose is a flexible metal tube that can run through an outside wall or up through the floor (don't change the floor's structural integrity). Keep it open at all times, and never let it penetrate a wall higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove — it must feed up into that channel.

The combustor carries two numbers: the certification label prints "Combustor OEM part number: Z0336A-M" (p. 4), and the combustor warranty section gives OEM Blaze King part # S.CAT203032 (p. 26), the number the parts list uses for the combustor assembly (p. 37).

Use only OEM gaskets from a Blaze King dealer, sized and ready to install — don't stretch or cut them. Door gasket: high temperature silicone adhesive, never household silicone; let it dry at least 1 hour, then do the paper test. Bypass gasket: OEM 5/8" fiber glass with THERMOSEAL® 1000F cement. Glass retainer screws: hand tight plus 1/4 turn. Combustor replacement: wait at least 12 hours after the last burn (a combustor can reach 1400F); a dealer or certified installer is recommended.

conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems, not a misprint: the certification label prints the 'Combustor OEM part number' Z0336A-M, while the combustor warranty section and parts list give OEM Blaze King part # S.CAT203032 (combustor assembly). The guide shows both and says what each is.

conflicts.issue: Fireplace installs: label says 'Not to be installed in any fireplace'; p. 13 bars alcove or fireplace installs in Canada only and tells USA installs to adhere to minimum safe clearances; p. 14 lists kits required for alcove installations.

Fan timing at start-up: Lighting step 7 says turn fan(s) on to high when the bypass is closed; step 11 says turn the fan on after the initial warm up; Fan Operation says fans off until normal operating temperature, then about 30 minutes after the fire is established match the thermostat setting.
Fan-off time before reading the catalytic thermometer: approximately 5 minutes (p. 18) vs 10 minutes (pp. 29, 35).

Vertical rise before the first elbow: 3 ft from stove top to elbow is 'recommended' for wall exits (p. 9); troubleshooting says 'make certain a minimum vertical rise of 36" is observed prior to elbows' (p. 36). The clearance drawing also carries 'MIN 2ft*' and '*3ft recommended' labels (pp. 4, 8) whose referent the text doesn't define.

Mobile home kits: pp. 4, 8 and 13 require an outside air kit plus a fan kit OR a rear shield kit; p. 14 describes the rear shield kit and the fan kit each as 'required for mobile home or alcove installations'.

review.notes: Single manual, 180-CK20.2 v3.01 (Feb 14, 2025). Figure-only content not transcribed, only pointed to: appliance dimensions (p. 7), usable firebox loading area (p. 19, shaded diagram), chimney installation drawings (p. 11), tested low burn thermostat setting (p. 22; its figure label extracts as unreadable glyphs and was not used). Warranty grid on p. 40: the parts/labor/wood columns can't be read reliably from the text, so the warranty drawer uses the p. 41 prose and p. 43 item 24 sliding scale. Clearances: the letters A-L, *1, *2 are defined only on the clearance drawing (pp. 4, 8); the guide lists the lettered values exactly as printed in the text tables without assigning meanings, and does not interpret the asterisks on C, D, F or drawing labels such as 'MIN 2ft*', '*3ft recommended', '2"(51 mm)'. Metric for 18" varies (450 mm in p. 8 text, 456 mm in p. 8 drawing labels, 457 mm on p. 4); the guide uses inches. Floor protection minimum size: p. 4 calls 32" x 40.125" (USA) / 41.375" x 50.125" (Canada) the minimum floor protection size, while p. 8 puts the same figures in the sentence about the shield under the chimney connector (UL 1618-2009 Type 1); both readings are shown in specFloor. Scrambled text decoded with the 29-code-point rule: p. 22 'milderI perhaps RRc to TMc ENP°` to ON°`FK' = 'milder, perhaps 55F to 70F (13°C to 21°C).' (used in the 'normal' drawer as 55F to 70F); p. 10 punctuation ('pipeK', 'roomI', '`himney J') decoded the same way; p. 10 figure label '$33/,$1&( &211(&725' (APPLIANCE CONNECTOR) not used. The catalog's 900-1500 sq ft heating area and 20-hour burn time are not stated anywhere in the manual, so they are unverified, not mismatches. The maker's website posts 'HHV Tested Efficiency 80.4%'; the manual names the B415.1-10 HHV method (p. 16) but prints no efficiency figure, so specOutput shows the website figure in a Maker's website note and it is listed in catalog_mismatches. website.json has no BTU or weight row for this model (product page gone), so the btu_output_min and weight_lb mismatches carry no Maker's website note. The cover's only French text points to French manuals online; no French-only safety block. No error-code table (codes empty). The fan kit is optional; fan guidance is folded into the lighting and controls drawers. The ash plug/ash drawer procedure is not described beyond the poker hook (p. 17) and season-end ash removal (p. 29).
